sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Georgie. Some kids hate eating broccoli.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔,我是乔治 有些孩子讨厌吃西兰花

sentences.en: For others, it's mushrooms. And worst of all, of course, are Brussels sprouts!
sentences.zh: 对其他人来说,是蘑菇,最糟糕的是布鲁塞尔芽!

sentences.en: Every parent of young children knows what food they will and won't eat.
sentences.zh: 每一个幼童的父母都知道他们会吃什么 也不会吃什么

sentences.en: What food did you dislike as a child, Georgie?
sentences.zh: 你小时候不喜欢什么食物,乔治?

sentences.en: Ooh, when I was little, I used to absolutely hate nuts and avocados.
sentences.zh: 哦,当我小的时候, 我曾经完全讨厌坚果和鳄梨。

sentences.en: But now, as an adult, I absolutely love both of those things.
sentences.zh: 但是现在,作为一个成年人, 我绝对爱这两个东西。

sentences.en: I'm not surprised – they're delicious! What about you, Neil?
sentences.zh: 我并不惊讶 它们很好吃 你呢,尼尔?

sentences.en: Did you dislike any foods? Do you know what?
sentences.zh: 你不喜欢吃东西吗?

sentences.en: I think I liked most things. Family dinner time can be fun – a chance to reconnect, hear about everyone's day and share a meal.
sentences.zh: 我想我喜欢大多数东西。 家庭晚餐时间会很有趣 — — 有机会重新连接,听到每个人的一天,分享一顿饭。

sentences.en: But when children refuse to eat the food that's been cooked, the result is often conflict rather than family fun.
sentences.zh: 但当孩子拒绝吃 烹饪的食物, 结果往往 冲突而不是家庭乐趣。

sentences.en: BBC Radio 4 programme The Food Chain asked child nutritionist and mother of two Charlotte Stirling-Reed whether her kids eat everything she gives them.
sentences.zh: 英国广播公司第4电台节目《食物链》问儿童营养师和两个夏洛特·斯特林-里德的母亲,她的孩子是否吃她给他们的一切。

sentences.en: They definitely don't. We go through multiple periods of ups and downs where their appetite is much lower, and then all of a sudden it comes right back.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定不会,我们经历了很多次 上下下,他们的食欲低得多, 然后突然间,它又回来了。

sentences.en: It depends on the weather, what they've been doing that day.
sentences.zh: 这取决于天气 那天他们在做什么

sentences.en: It can depend on their mood. At dinner time, Charlotte's children go through ups and downs, a phrase meaning that a mixture of good and bad things happen to them.
sentences.zh: 夏洛特的孩子在晚饭时上下上下下上下下下下, 这句话的意思是,好坏事会发生在他们身上。

sentences.en: Sometimes they eat everything happily. Other times they don't.
sentences.zh: 有时他们快乐地吃东西,有时他们不快乐

sentences.en: It depends on many things, including their day, the weather and their mood.
sentences.zh: 这取决于许多事情 包括白天 天气和心情

sentences.en: A person's mood is the way they are feeling at a particular time.
sentences.zh: 一个人的情绪是他们在某个时候的感觉。

sentences.en: So, how can parents make dinnertime something everyone enjoys?
sentences.zh: 那么,父母怎么能做饭时间 每个人都喜欢的东西呢?

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll be hearing from three experts on young children's eating habits and learning some useful new words and phrases too.
sentences.zh: 在这一集中,我们将会听到 三个关于幼儿饮食习惯的专家 并且学习一些有用的新词和新词。

sentences.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary from this episode, along with a quiz and worksheet, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 并记住,你会发现所有词汇 从这集, 连同测验和工作表, 在我们的网站,bbclearingenglish.com。

sentences.en: But first of course, Georgie, I have a question for you.
sentences.zh: 但首先 乔治 我有个问题要问你

sentences.en: Charlotte Stirling-Reed is a child nutritionist and she has some tips for stress-free family meals.
sentences.zh: Charlotte Stirling-Reed是一名儿童营养学家,她有一些关于家庭无压力餐的提示。

sentences.en: Which of these do you think she recommends?
sentences.zh: 你觉得她推荐哪个?

sentences.en: Is it: a) make sure your child eats five pieces of fruit and veg a day, b) don't pressure your child to eat everything on the plate, or c) introduce your child to lots of new flavours quickly?
sentences.zh: 是:(a) 确保你的孩子每天吃五片水果和蔬菜;(b) 不强迫你的孩子吃盘子上的所有东西;或(c) 很快地将你的孩子介绍给许多新的口味?

sentences.en: That's quite hard. They all seem like quite good tips.
sentences.zh: 很难,他们看起来都是很好的小费

sentences.en: I'm going to go with c) introduce your child to lots of new flavours quickly.
sentences.zh: 我要和C一起 很快地给你的孩子 介绍一些新的口味

sentences.en: OK. We'll find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的 我们稍后在节目里会找出答案的

sentences.en: Dr Anne Fishel is another expert in child nutrition.
sentences.zh: Anne Fishel博士是儿童营养方面的另一位专家。

sentences.en: She co-founded the Family Dinner Project, an organisation promoting children's healthy eating in the US.
sentences.zh: 她共同创建了家庭晚餐项目,这是一个促进美国儿童健康饮食的组织。

sentences.en: Here, Anne explains one reason why mealtimes can become stressful, to Ruth Alexander for BBC World Service programme The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: Anne向英国广播公司世界服务节目《食物链》的Ruth Alexander解释,

sentences.en: Many parents say dinnertime can become a battleground, so why is it that what you're eating can trigger so much tension?
sentences.zh: 很多家长说晚餐时间会变成战场 所以为什么你吃的东西会引发这么多紧张?

sentences.en: I think for small children it's one of the few areas that they have control over.
sentences.zh: 我想对于小孩子来说,这是他们能控制的少数领域之一。

sentences.en: I mean, parents can cook what they want and serve it when they want, but it's up to kids to decide whether they're going to eat it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是,父母可以烹饪他们想要的东西 并在他们想要的时候服务它, 但由孩子们来决定 他们是否要吃它。

sentences.en: And for young kids, that's a big deal. They have some control.
sentences.zh: 对小孩子来说,这很重要,他们有控制力

sentences.en: Dinnertime often becomes a battleground – a place where argument or conflict happens.
sentences.zh: 晚餐时间往往成为战场 — — 发生争吵或冲突的地方。

sentences.en: Anne thinks that's because it's one of the few areas where children have control.
sentences.zh: Anne认为那是因为 这是孩子们能控制的少数地区之一

sentences.en: For kids, controlling what they're willing to eat is a big deal – something of special importance to them.
sentences.zh: 对于孩子来说,控制他们愿意吃的东西是一件大事 对他们来说特别重要的事

sentences.en: If experts like Charlotte and Anne struggle at mealtimes, imagine how hard it could be if your child has a food allergy – a condition where the body makes you sick after eating certain foods.
sentences.zh: 如果像夏洛特和安妮这样的专家在吃饭时挣扎, 想象一下,如果你的孩子过敏—— 一种身体在吃某些食物后会生病的情况—— 可能会有多难。

sentences.en: That was the experience of Sharon Wee, a food writer from Singapore, who speaks here with BBC World Service programme The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: 这是新加坡一位食品作家Sharon Wee的经验,他在英国广播公司世界服务节目《食物链》上发言。

sentences.en: My daughter was born with allergies and it was quite a struggle at first.
sentences.zh: 我女儿生来过敏 一开始很挣扎

sentences.en: And to be honest with you, we found the winning formula, which was rice and beans, and she grew up eating rice and beans probably for the first five years of her life.
sentences.zh: 说实话,我们找到了获胜的公式, 即大米和豆子, 她长大后吃大米和豆子 可能是她生命的头五年。

sentences.en: Sharon's daughter's allergies restricted what she could eat, making cooking for the whole family a struggle.
sentences.zh: 莎伦的女儿过敏 限制了她能吃的东西 使整个家族的烹饪成为一种斗争

sentences.en: Luckily, Sharon discovered the winning formula – something her daughter could safely eat – rice and beans.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是,沙龙发现了获胜的配方——她女儿可以安全地吃的东西——大米和豆子。

sentences.en: A winning formula is a method or strategy that produces successful results.
sentences.zh: 获胜的公式是产生成功结果的方法或战略。

sentences.en: So, Georgie, how can parents help their children develop good eating habits?
sentences.zh: Georgie 父母如何帮助孩子养成良好的饮食习惯?

sentences.en: Well, there are some things that our experts all agree upon.
sentences.zh: 我们的专家都同意一些事情

sentences.en: For one, give children a choice – for example, by offering small, healthy snacks and dips before the meal.
sentences.zh: 首先,给儿童一个选择,例如,在饭前提供小型、健康的零食和泡菜。

sentences.en: And most importantly of all, create a stress-free atmosphere by not pressurising kids to finish everything on their plate.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是 创造一个没有压力的氛围 通过不给孩子施压 完成他们盘子上的一切

sentences.en: Right. Well, that also helps with your quiz question, Neil, so why not go ahead and reveal the correct answer?
sentences.zh: 好吧,那也有助于你的测验问题,尼尔, 为什么不继续 并揭示正确的答案?

sentences.en: I asked you what child food nutritionist Charlotte Stirling-Reed recommends for stress-free family meals.
sentences.zh: 我问你 儿童食物营养学家 夏洛特・斯特林 -里德 推荐 免费家庭餐。

sentences.en: Yes. I said c) introduce your child to lots of new flavours quickly.
sentences.zh: 是的,我说,C) 把你的孩子介绍给很多新的香料。

sentences.en: I'm afraid you were wrong, Georgie. The answer is actually b) don't pressure your child to eat everything on the plate.
sentences.zh: 恐怕你错了 乔治 答案是b) 不要强迫你的孩子吃盘子里的东西

sentences.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with ups and downs – a phrase describing the mixture of good and bad things that happen to someone.
sentences.zh: 好吧,让我们回顾一下我们所学的词汇,从上到下开始-- 这句话描述了发生在某人身上的善与恶的混合。

sentences.en: Your mood is how you feel at a particular time.
sentences.zh: 你的心情是你在某个时候的感觉

sentences.en: A battleground is a place or situation where argument or conflict happens.
sentences.zh: 战场是争论或冲突发生的地方或情况。

sentences.en: If something is a big deal, it's of special importance to you.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么大不了的 这对你很重要

sentences.en: A food allergy is a medical condition where certain foods make your body sick.
sentences.zh: 食物过敏是一种医疗状况 某些食物让你的身体生病

sentences.en: And finally, a winning formula is a method or strategy that produces successful results.
sentences.zh: 最后,获胜的公式是产生成功结果的方法或战略。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to learn more vocabulary on the topic of food, you can head to our topic page on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 再一次,我们的六分钟到了, 但如果你想学习更多关于食物主题的词汇, 你可以去我们网站的主题网页,bbc学习英语. com。

sentences.en: See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 很快再见,但现在再见了

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见!
